result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers separate the table from the dashboard sentences and recommend right-aligned tabular lining figures for the table. B's CSS is more careful: it right-aligns only the numeric columns, while A also right-aligns the description column and makes old-style figures the global default on body. B also explains what happens when a font lacks the figure styles (the setting is silently ignored) and gives a concrete test, while A covers font support well but gives no way to check it. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers use tabular lining figures for the table and proportional figures for the dashboard sentences. Answer A has cleaner CSS because it right-aligns only the numeric columns, while Answer B right-aligns every table cell, including descriptions. Answer B is more candid about font support: it notes Inter's limited old-style figures and the risk that font subsetting drops these features, and it offers a font-feature-settings fallback. That roughly balances A's tidier code.
